stories.title: Democrats claim Republican strongholds in midterm victory
stories.summary: Democrats have seized control of both the Senate and House, scoring sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations as tens of millions of voters delivered a scathing rebuke to President Donald Trump. Voters in conservative bastions who had propelled the president to his second term in office just two years ago swung dramatically toward Democrats, fueled by deep frustration over the unpopular war with Iran, anxiety over the high cost of living and anger at Mr Trump's stewardship of the country. In Kansas, Adam Hamilton, a megachurch pastor, became the first Democrat to win a Senate seat since the Great Depression nearly a century ago. And in Texas, the biggest Republican state, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning a Senate seat and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott. In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown claimed a seat that belonged to Vice President JD Vance two years ago. Both Ohio and Texas voted for Mr Trump by a double-digit margin in 2024.

stories.title: AIB ups full year guidance for customer loans, deposits
stories.summary: AIB has raised its full year guidance for its customer loans and deposits as well as its net interest income after it reported another strong quarter on the back of the resilience of the economy and the continued momentum in the business. In a trading update for the third quarter of 2026, AIB said its total income rose by 3%, while gross loans grew by 5.6% to €76.3 billion from €72.3 billion at the end of last December. The bank said its gross loans are now expected to grow by 5-6%, up from its previous guidance of around 5%. Total new lending for the nine months to the end of September increased by 17% to €12.3 billion, with its new mortage lending in Ireland up 4% at €3.2 billion, which indicated a market share of 28.4%. Meanwhile, new lending to Irish SMEs increased to €1.2 billion, the bank noted. AIB said its net interest income (NII) rose by 2% to €2.87 billion in the nine months to September, compared to the same time last year, mainly due to higher average volumes.

stories.title: Man killed as helicopters collide in Nepal near Everest
stories.summary: An Indian tourist was killed and another tourist from New Zealand was brought to hospital after two helicopters collided and crashed while attempting to land in Nepal's Everest region. Authorities said the Fishtail Air and Dynasty Air helicopters' rotor blades struck each other as they were attempting to land around 8.11am (2.26am Irish time) at Pheriche Helipad in Solukhumbu. Another passenger on the same aircraft, a New Zealand citizen, was injured in the collision and was taken to hospital. Both pilots also sustained minor injuries and were taken to Kathmandu for further medical treatment. Authorities have yet to establish the total number of passengers who were on board the two helicopters at the time of the crash. Small helicopters are widely used in the Himalayan nation to transport tourists, climbers and supplies, as well as to carry out emergency evacuations.

stories.title: Carrick 'proud' but not getting carried away
stories.summary: Under-fire Michael Carrick is not getting carried away with Manchester United's wild comeback win against Roma despite acknowledging the importance of the 3-2 triumph to his misfiring squad’s confidence. Old Trafford witnessed an incredible conclusion to a Champions League night that began with fresh protests against owners the Glazer family and the visitors punishing a first-half display that was as meek as it was shambolic. Matias Soule’s avoidable opener was followed by a Donyell Malen penalty as United fans once again booed their team at the break, only for Carrick’s side to dig deep and produce an unforgettable turnaround. Skipper Bruno Fernandes converted a retaken penalty before Matheus Cunha scored a last-gasp brace – and picked up an even later sending-off – as the Red Devils ended their nine-match winless run in style. "Proud of a lot of people, actually," United head coach Carrick said. "Proud of the players. I think they deserve a lot of credit for pulling through that in a tough situation. "And for the supporters, you know, to be there. I could feel they were desperate for us to give them something to get their teeth into.

stories.title: RTÉ Supporting The Arts this November
stories.summary: Film fans can enjoy a host of international and Irish films this month with the 71st Cork International Film Festival, the Peugeot IFI French Film Festival, the Waterford International Film Festival and the Dingle Film Festival all taking place throughout November. These festivals will bring together filmmakers, industry professionals and audiences to experience the very best of Irish and international cinema right across the country. In the world of theatre, LemonSoap Productions's Beards and Once Off's take on The Seagull by Anton Chekhov will both grace the stage of Dublin's Smock Alley Theatre while Pan Pan Theatre present Long Day's Journey, Glass Mask Theatre present the world premiere of The Last Pagans by Stephen Jones and James Joyce's The Dead returns to the Museum of Literature Ireland for a third year. Meanwhile, the Gate Theatre will stage a production of It's a Wonderful Life while the Abbey Theatre presents a packed programme of four productions, from ANIMALS to The Magnificent. The Irish National Opera also presents a highly anticipated tour of Bizet's Carmen. Dance audiences will be treated to a varied programme featuring Ballet Ireland's nationwide tour of Romeo & Juliet, CoisCéim's SINGSONG by David Bolger, and LUAIL's nationwide presentation of Nōs. Together, these productions showcase contemporary and classical approaches to movement and storytelling on stages across the country. A wide range of exhibitions and showcases are available for art fans in November including IMMA Collection: Art as Agency, Technologies of Peace: Art and Transition in Contemporary Europe (1989–2026), Hilma af Klint: Artist and Visionary at the National Gallery of Ireland, Una Sealy: Time Lines at RHA Gallery, the RDS Visual Art Awards, and Julián - a Butler Gallery & Cartoon Saloon Exhibition in Kilkenny. These events will celebrate and highlight the breadth of contemporary and historical art on display throughout Ireland. Lemonsoap\u0027s Beards comes to Dublin\u0027s Smock Alley Theatre

stories.title: West Cork couple tie the knot in surprise wedding on US chat show
stories.summary: Most couple's nuptials are presided over by a parish priest or maybe even a close friend or relative, but for one West Cork couple, theirs was led by none other than an Oscar-winning star. Amanda Murnane and Brendan Hayes, a couple from Bantry, became the first couple to wed on The Jennifer Hudson Show last month, in a surprise ceremony that was officiated by the bubbly host herself. The couple have a long love story, having been together for 27 years and sharing three children, Rene, Clarice and Michael, and one grandson, Wayne. Both have spent years working for West Cork Mental Health Services, while Brendan is also an independent filmmaker, documentary maker, writer, actor and director. Although they had long wanted to get married, a number of obstacles held them back, most notably in 2011 when their daughter Rene was diagnosed with leukemia. While Rene eventually overcame that health setback, that period of their lives was marked by stress and difficulty, which led Brendan to wanting to give Amanda something positive. Their story got another cinematic twist on 23 October when Brendan surprised Amanda with an elaborately planned wedding on stage, in front of a live studio audience. The plan was hatched over months, with Brendan secretly arranging the surprise alongside the show's production team.

stories.title: Blue tsunami: Victory washes over Democrats in midterms
stories.summary: This election can be described by the text I got from a high-ranking official in the Republican Party: a bloodbath. Even voters in areas that have repeatedly backed US President Donald Trump are no longer on board with the Republican Party. Within an hour of the first polls closing, the first signs emerged that it was going to be a good night for the Democrats, when major US networks called the Senate race in Georgia for incumbent Senator Jon Ossoff. Georgia was a top priority for Democrats, who needed to hold the seat to stay on course for a Senate majority. Astonishingly, just a year ago, Mr Ossoff was described by CNN as "the nation's most endangered Senate Democrat". He was considered particularly vulnerable as an incumbent running in a state that Mr Trump had won in 2024.

stories.title: Spanish police dismantle Madrid housing protest camp
stories.summary: Police have dismantled a sprawling tent camp in Madrid which had spearheaded protests over Spain's housing crisis for more than a month and prompted early elections, police and activists said. Officers closed off much of the Spanish capital's emblematic Puerta del Sol square this morning as municipal cleaning staff swept away remaining debris, tents and tarpaulin. The Madrid camp sprang up in September, after Spain's chronic housing crisis burst into the centre of public debate following the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong Madrid home. The eviction sparked nationwide protests against runaway housing costs and a lack of tenant protections, with tens of thousands of demonstrators hitting the streets. The Madrid camp has since mushroomed into a sprawling warren of tents and tarpaulin that hosted hundreds of people in a mini-city equipped with a canteen, a clinic and a space for meetings. This morning, the central government's delegation in the Madrid region said the eviction took place overnight "without incident or episodes of violence", reporting that 334 people were removed and two arrested.

stories.title: Amond: It's been a long time - even I wasn't born
stories.summary: Waterford FC captain Padraig Amond hailed manager Graham Coughlan as "the catalyst" for the revival in the club's fortunes and said it had been too long since they brought silverware back to the south-east. Having finally made sure of their survival in the Premier Division last weekend, Amond and co face Derry City in Sunday's FAI Cup final, the first time that Waterford have reached the decider since 2004. That final in the old Lansdowne Road looked to be heading in the Blues' direction, with future Ireland international Daryl Murphy flicking a header on for Willie Bruton to put them in front with 25 minutes remaining. stories.title: KIDS Book Club: Travel back in time with historical fiction
stories.summary: As 2026 comes to a close and we look towards the near future of 2027, there are so many technological advances, social changes and big moments that have shaped and shifted our world this year. While we certainly can't predict the future, there is one way we can revisit our past and it doesn’t involve inventing a time machine! Historical fiction is a fantastic way to travel through time and experience how the world has changed in a unique way. For better or worse, we can see how technology has changed, remember interesting historical figures, see the progress of Ireland or even experience the discovery of new world cultures. History buffs, this month’s book club is for you – enjoy travelling through time with some fantastic stories. The Flying Feminist by Mary Boone, illustrated by Andrea Turk, Andersen Press, 32PP ISBN 9781839135101 This picturebook is based on the true story of the amazing Lilian Bland, the first woman to design, build and even fly her own airplane in 1910. Lilian’s story is one of bravery, tenacity, and the absolute refusal to give up on herself, even when everyone else had.

stories.title: Bella Maclean put no nudity clause into Rivals contract
stories.summary: Actress Bella Maclean has said she put a no nudity clause into her contract on Disney+ drama Rivals. The 28-year-old plays Taggie O'Hara in the show, which follows the world of independent television in 1986, and follows a rivalry between Lord Tony Baddingham (David Tennant) and former MP Rupert Campbell-Black (Alex Hassell). Speaking about adding the clause, she told Harper’s Bazaar: "It was important because of how pure Taggie’s character was. I didn’t want to sexually exploit her, and I didn’t want to do that to myself either. "That was really important to me, and I think it will stay important to me. There are some things I just want to keep to myself. "I don’t judge anyone who does it. Sometimes it’s so beautiful. If I had Victoria Smurfit’s body, I’d probably be walking around naked. "But in that sense, we’re all lucky because there are amazing intimacy coordinators on our job. I know that’s not the case for other people. We’re all good friends who can just say no to the directors and they’ll listen."

She suggests getting creative with your meal planning to clear out as much freezer food as possible before Christmas. "This will help you save money [on food] that you can repurpose towards your Christmas budget, and will also free up room in the freezer for all of the festive goodies that will come in," explains Bray.

stories.title: Top takeaways from the US midterm elections
stories.summary: Democrats have taken control of Congress in US midterm elections, making extraordinary gains deep in Republican territory with voters delivering a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump and his agenda. Opinion polls ahead of the midterms pointed to Democrats having a good night. But the scale of their gains was far greater than most analysts had forecast, extending beyond traditional battlegrounds deep into Republican territory. In Texas, James Talarico routed Republican Ken Paxton, becoming the state's first Democratic senator-elect in 38 years. In flipping the Senate seat in South Carolina, the party also made history. Democrats have not won a US Senate race there this century, and the win by Annie Andrews over Republican Senator Darline Graham became another defining upset of the night. In the Senate race in Ohio, a state Mr Trump won three times, Democrat Sherrod Brown prevailed, while in Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton easily defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall. Democrats last won a Senate seat in Kansas in 1932, during the Great Depression. Democrats were projected by US media outlets to win back control of both the US House and Senate.

stories.title: Stocks, dollar slide as wins for Democrats jolt AI bets
stories.summary: Global stocks fell and the dollar hit a one-month low today as Democrats gained control of both the Senate and the House in the US midterm elections, fuelling fears that rapid AI sector growth could be hamstrung by regulatory scrutiny. In a major setback to President Donald Trump, Democrats notched up victories in the South Carolina, Texas and Ohio Senate races, capturing majorities in both the Senate and House that reached deep into Republican strongholds. The breadth of the party's success was underscored by gains in districts long considered safely conservative, highlighting a political shift that caught many investors off guard. stories.title: Cunha sees red but caps quickfire comeback win over Roma
stories.summary: Matheus Cunha's late brace secured Manchester United a jaw-dropping 3-2 comeback win against Roma to breathe new life into their season and ease some of the pressure on Michael Carrick. A nine-match winless run had left the Red Devils head coach’s job hanging by a thread and Tuesday’s wretched start in the Champions League only pushed him closer to the Old Trafford exit. United were facing a fourth straight loss after Matias Soule’s avoidable opener was followed up by a Donyell Malen penalty in a first half that ended with boos. Green and gold balloons had cascaded down the Stretford End as fans protested against the Glazers before the match, with the second half offering a reminder of the special spirit that underpins their club. Bruno Fernandes pulled one back from a retaken, and softly awarded, second-half spot-kick as United played with the kind of purpose and skill lacking this term. That approach forced a late error that Cunha capitalised on, before the Brazil forward slammed in off the inside of the near post for the winner.

stories.title: Traffic disruption expected in capital during EU meetings
stories.summary: Dublin will experience significant disruption for four days next week as the largest policing operation in the history of the State takes place as part of Ireland's EU Presidency. European leaders are meeting in the capital next Thursday and Friday but the security operation around these events, which has been described as "unprecedented" will get under way two days before, on Tuesday 10 November. Anyone travelling to or around the capital, between Tuesday and Friday next week, is being warned to plan their journeys and expect major and prolonged traffic disruption. Around 50 European leaders are due to attend meetings of the European political community in the Convention Centre on Dublin's North Wall Quay next Thursday and Friday. A dinner for visiting leaders will also take place in the National Gallery on Merrion Square on Thursday evening. These summits are the largest ever meetings of heads of state or government in Ireland and gardaí say their scale and complexity are a significant logistical undertaking with unprecedented security considerations.

stories.title: McNamara appointment 'great news' for Leinster - Keenan
stories.summary: Leinster full-back Hugo Keenan has hailed the "exciting appointment" of Noel McNamara as the province's next head coach. The Clare native, who spent five years at Leinster between 2016 and 2021 in a variety of development roles, will succeed Leo Cullen as head coach next summer. While McNamara has never been head coach at senior level, the 43-year-old spent two years as head coach of Ireland's Under-20 team between 2019 and 2021, while he has most recently helped Bordeaux-Begles to successive Investec Champions Cup titles. "I think it's great news, I've got a good relationship with him," Keenan said of this morning's announcement. "I would have worked with him in the past, both at UCD originally, he was the head coach there when I was playing AIL, when I was sort of between the Academy and Sevens and playing AIL rugby, and then dealt with them as well for the 'A' team in Leinster, and know him well. "Obviously that was a couple of years ago, and he's progressed so well since.

stories.summary: Last month, Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport Patrick O'Donovan confirmed that the broadcaster is to receive less funding than envisaged in Budget 2027 due to his dissatisfaction with what he called the broadcaster's progress in implementing promised reforms last month. He will say in his opening statement that "public funding carries an obligation to continue to demonstrate value, accountability and delivery". He will say the multi-annual funding provided "essential stability" to the broadcaster, adding this stability was used to strengthen governance and financial discipline. The "work of transformation is far from over", the Director General will tell TDs. He will point towards "tangible signs of progress, including in the services and content we provide to audiences all over Ireland" two years into its 'New Direction' strategy. Mr Ó Coigligh will point towards competing demands for funding across the department.

stories.title: Raphinha rampant as Barcelona overwhelm Aston Villa
stories.summary: Barcelona ensured Unai Emery had another Nou Camp nightmare as they beat his Aston Villa side 3-0 in the Champions League. Lamine Yamal's early opener and a second-half double for Europe’s most prolific scorer Raphinha, who has bagged 19 in 13 games this season, gave Emery a 55th birthday to forget. The Spaniard will not be keen to return to this city any time soon as he has now lost 15 out of 16 matches at Barca, including the famous 'Remontada’ nine years ago, when his PSG side lost a last-16 tie 6-1 to squander a 4-0 first-leg lead. This was supposed to be a Red Letter Day for the club – a reward for their excellent progress in the four years of Emery’s reign. It might have been more memorable had Villa taken a number of first-half chances to draw level, but defeat ends their 100% start to the league phase. stories.summary: Minister for Enterprise Peter Burke is seeking to put a maximum compensation cap on the amount that people can claim in minor injury cases. Mr Burke believes that the costs involved in some compensation cases here are disproportionately higher than in several other countries. This issue was discussed in recent days at a Cabinet sub-committee meeting on insurance reform. A similar cap in England and Wales was introduced in 2018 on compensation claims for whiplash and soft tissue damage lasting up to 24 months.

stories.title: Connolly: The pundits are backing Waterford to win it
stories.summary: Derry City interim-manager Mark Connolly says the majority of pundits are backing Waterford in Sunday's Club Orange Men's FAI Cup final but he's confident his team are entering the decider in a buoyant frame of mind on the back of a difficult year. The Candystripes endured an incredibly turbulent first half of the season, marred by the saga over James McClean's unhappy return to the club and their disastrous drop-off in form in the league. Connolly, a Cup winner with the club in 2022, had returned as Director of Football at the beginning of the season. When Tiernan Lynch was sacked as manager at the start of August, the 34-year old was installed as interim manager despite not possessing a UEFA Pro Licence. Notwithstanding the lack of paperwork, he has overseen a transformation in form at Derry. While their long-touted league ambitions were already shot to pieces, they finished the campaign in decent form and this has been accompanied by another surge in the Cup. They dispatched Dundalk 4-2 in the quarter-finals and it was after the 2-0 win away to Galway United in the semi-final, that Connolly fully believed that the club were back in tune with their supporters. "This season as a whole has been a difficult one," Connolly told reporters at Tuesday's press conference.

stories.title: Talks to continue over dispute on public sector pay deal
stories.summary: Trade unions and Government representatives will hold further separate talks today with an independent body in a bid to resolve the ongoing dispute over public sector pay. Engagement began yesterday with a Government appointed group chaired by Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) Chair Kevin Foley. A spokesperson for the Department of Public Expenditure said the process remains under way, with both parties asked to undertake further consideration of the matters being discussed. "Officials will continue to make themselves available to engage intensively and constructively in this process, with a view to resolving matters without undue delay," the department said. On Monday, unions announced plans for a 24-hour strike on Thursday 12 November. They have accused the Government of failing to make a credible offer on pay.

stories.title: Champions Lge round-up: Bayern tame Atleti, PSG run riot
stories.summary: Paris Saint-Germain produced another stunning Champions League display in a 6-0 rout of Villarreal to move three points clear at the top of the table. Harry Kane missed out on equalling Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of scoring in 11 consecutive Champions League matches in Bayern Munich’s 2-0 win at Atletico Madrid. PSG delivered another statement win in as Fabian Ruiz struck twice in Spain as Villarreal were the latest side to be put to the sword. Luis Enrique’s side, who made it 10 straight wins, were 4-0 up inside 17 minutes, with Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Ruiz all on target. Ruiz put PSG 5-0 up early in the second half and substitute David Boly completed the scoring in the 78th minute. England skipper Kane, appearing in his first European tie since winning the Ballon d’Or, had scored in his previous 10 Champions League appearances, but drew a rare blank as second-half goals from teenager Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer sealed victory in Madrid.

stories.title: 55% rise in demand for women's addiction service - report
stories.summary: There was significant demand for Merchant Quay Ireland's (MQI) dedicated women's service last year, according to its latest annual review. Those who sought help for addiction and homelessness at Jane's Place rose by 55% between 2024 and 2025. It highlights a significant need for accessible day support services, according to the charity. Having spent a decade living abroad, Philomena returned to Ireland in recent years at the height of her addiction to alcohol, cocaine, prescription tablets and cannabis. "It took over my life, and it came to the point where I walked out on my children, and I broke my marriage and I got myself into very dangerous situations. "I was in a mental hospital, and I was in a foreign country, so I had to come back, or I was going to die," she says.

stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Johnny Kenny was forced off in the first half of Preston's 3-2 defeat to Sheffield United at Deepdale after suffering a hamstring injury. Kenny joined Preston from Celtic on a permanent deal on transfer deadline day and has since gone on to score two goals in eight Championship appearances. Sydie Peck was the difference-maker in the game as he bagged a first-half hat-trick for Sheffield United. stories.title: Legal aid changes 'unfair, illogical', High Court finds
stories.summary: The High Court has found that new regulations brought in by Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan to govern the payment of legal aid in criminal cases are "grossly unfair" and "demonstrably illogical". The new regulations providing for a flat fee of €520 to be paid per accused person, regardless of the number of charges against them or the number of court appearances, are at the centre of a dispute between the minister and criminal legal aid solicitors which has disrupted the criminal justice system for more than four months. Solicitor John Quinn challenged the new regulations in a judicial review. Mr Quinn, and the solicitors' representative body, the Law Society, who were notice parties to the case, argued the new regulations were unlawful as they provided for the certification and payment of legal aid in a way that went beyond the legislation. In her ruling, Ms Justice Mary Rose Gearty said the provision in the new scheme of a single payment to a solicitor when the final order in the case is made is "grossly unfair". The minister has since tweaked the scheme, allowing for two-thirds of the fee to be paid at the beginning of the case and the remainder at the end of the case or after 12 months.

stories.title: Spain's transport minister resigns days after train crash
stories.summary: Spain's transport minister, Oscar Puente, has announced his resignation over last week's deadly train crash, the country's second this year, hours after laying out the government's emergency aid package for victims and new safety measures. "A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot continue in office with two accidents of this severity in less than a year," he told lawmakers of the Permanent Deputation, a standing committee that sits when parliament is dissolved. He spoke nearly a week after the 28 October crash that killed 69 people near the town of Urda in central Spain. His departure comes less than four weeks before an early parliamentary election that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez calledfor 29 November, and after two deadly crashes on the same line this ‌year. Mr Sanchez praised Mr Puente in a post on ⁠X, thanking him for his work and saying the minister had put victims first and acted out of a sense of political responsibility. Mr Puente, who had previously ruled out resigning, said he had decided to step down within minutes of learning of the crash, but chose to remain in office until the immediate emergency response was under way, preliminary investigations had begun and the first measures to compensate victims and improve rail safety had been put in place.

stories.title: Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel dies after on-field collision
stories.summary: Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club have announced. The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge 30-year-old striker De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second tier game. The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: "Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda. "There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness. "We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones…that today weep for this cruel outcome. The family of Jesus de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments." Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as "stable despite the severity of his condition".
